facts.text: I'm hungry, I'm homesick, and I want pizza. Pass me whatever is hot and let's get back to New York.
facts.why: Raphael never says this. The pizza line on the quote page belongs to Michelangelo ('d'you think they had pizza back then?').
facts.fix: Awesome! But d'you think they had pizza back then?

fix_note.text: Awesome! But d'you think they had pizza back then?

facts.text: Serve the mains when the turtles realise there's no pizza in 1603.
facts.why: The quote page has Mikey wondering if they had pizza back then before they leave. A synopsis opened has Michelangelo introducing the villagers to pizza in the past. Nothing shows them realising there is none.
facts.fix: Serve the mains when Mikey asks if they had pizza back in 1603.

facts.text: Casey Jones along for the ride
facts.why: Casey stays in present day New York with Splinter and Kenshin. He does not travel to 1603.
facts.fix: Casey Jones minding Kenshin back in New York

vibe.verdict: The feudal village idea works, but the poster sits in big black bars on parchment and the pizza gag misses the film's real jokes.
missing: Michelangelo introducing the villagers to pizza
Splinter's Elvis impression at the end
Casey teaching the Honor Guard hockey
The turtles disguised as honour guards

Replace the black-barred poster with a full-bleed still.
